tayla.devex: Running into inconsistent SSL behavior with the Python SDK when using Dedicated + corp proxy + custom CA. Sometimes the call stalls; sometimes it raises ssl.SSLCertVerificationError.
ken.eng-runtime: Is this the async client or sync? Async uses aiohttp which expects ssl.SSLContext if you pass verify as a path.
sam.platform: We also force trust_env=False in the transport to avoid leaked proxies for hosted. That breaks customers behind corporate proxies for Dedicated.
tayla.devex: Repro (async):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., base_url='https://dedicated.acme.internal', verify='/etc/certs/corp-ca.pem')
await client.chat.create(...)
```
With HTTPS_PROXY set it sometimes hangs ~20s then errors. Unsetting HTTPS_PROXY makes it succeed.
ken.eng-runtime: Quick plan: 1) normalize `verify` into SSLContext in a shared helper used by sync+async; 2) add client option `trust_env_proxies` (default False for hosted, True for dedicated/private) so aiohttp uses trust_env accordingly; 3) improve logs to distinguish proxy handshake timeout vs cert verify.
sam.platform: Add tests: unit for cafile vs capath parity, and a CI integration using mitmproxy to simulate TLS interception. Also document NO_PROXY recommendations in Dedicated onboarding.
tayla.devex: Acceptance: async+sync parity, proxy env toggle, clearer errors, CI mitmproxy repro. I'll share a tiny docker-compose for mitmproxy to validate.
